summary:
We developed Apogee, an educational RPG built in Godot where players step into the boots of a Terranova Agency astronaut to experience the full lifecycle of a real space mission.

To address the NASA Space Apps challenge, Apogee turns mission planning into hands-on gameplay. Players choose missions inspired by true NASA history, calculate launch parameters—including altitude, inclination, and circularity via GMAT—design their spacecraft, make instant decisions during real-data space emergencies, and conclude with a scientific mission report.

Apogee is important because space science often feels overly complicated and out of reach for people. By transforming real NASA data into an interactive, high-stakes adventure, Apogee demystifies aerospace engineering, sparks curiosity in astronomy, and helps inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Apogee is an educational space-mission RPG developed in Godot using GDScript that puts players in the boots of an astronaut working for the fictional Terranova Agency. Designed to make space exploration approachable for teenagers, the game guides players through the full lifecycle of a mission modeled directly on real NASA operations, including Apollo 7, Artemis II, and the International Space Station (ISS) expeditions.


Gameplay

Gameplay begins before liftoff, where players customize their spacecraft and calculate essential launch parameters, such as altitude, inclination, and orbital circularity using GMAT to establish an accurate flight trajectory. Once in orbit, players confront unpredictable, real-world hazards and technical complications drawn from authentic NASA mission logs. Rather than reducing spaceflight to simple right-or-wrong trivia, Apogee challenges players to weigh trade-offs and make the best strategic decisions for their ship and crew's safety, concluding each mission with a comprehensive scientific flight report.


Accuracy

At its core, Apogee blends the storytelling and charm of a pixel-art RPG crafted using GameMaker’s sprite interface. Our team carefully balanced scientific rigor with accessibility: we investigated actual emergencies faced by astronauts and distilled those technical scenarios into clear, intuitive choices without sacrificing real-world logic. By combining a clean, uncluttered interface with authentic GMAX trajectory modeling, the game replaces passive reading with active problem-solving.


Why Apogee as a science outreach method?

Astronomy and orbital mechanics often feel overly complicated and intimidating to young audiences, resulting in low engagement with space science. By transforming authentic NASA data into an interactive, high-stakes adventure, Apogee demystifies how space missions actually work, builds critical thinking under pressure, and aims to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
